title: Dispatch GID 7: Searchers Prepare to Close the Instrument for Good
summary: The plate will face a blank wall once the missing attendant reaches the aisle.
author: Clara Vale, Staff Correspondent
paragraphs: A controlled operation is scheduled for tomorrow evening at the Lyceum. Dr. Saye and Miss Marsh will raise the silvered plate for no more than three minutes. Inspector Voss will watch the rear aisle. Dr. Halden will stand at the plate’s turning wheel, which can swing it toward a blank wall without disturbing the lamp.

The plan follows measurements taken from the closed auditorium. The extra chair impressions point toward the plate even when its cover is in place. Turning it away should end the line of sight that allows the second audience to gather. Dr. Saye says this is a test, not a certainty.

Ruth Crain will sit where her sister last saw the unfamiliar passage. She has brought a small handbell used by the stage staff to signal a clear aisle. Its note was recorded before the trial so searchers can distinguish it from any sound made through the instrument.

Dr. Halden spoke at a short press conference. “I brought people here to show them another world,” he said. “I did not know that a view could be kept open after we left.” He has surrendered his notes to the Institute and says he will turn the plate himself when Miss Marsh gives the word.

The Lyceum’s public doors will be locked during the operation. This newspaper has been permitted to observe from the balcony. Inspector Voss asked those without duties to remain away from the building. Reports of a second audience have drawn crowds to the street each evening.
